creator: Alexander Terp
description:
A person running fifteen agents wants to say which is which in their own
words - "🔥 payments spike", "🧪 flaky test hunt" - rather than reading
directories. Pairs with a_292vXFFHn (agent subtext); the two decide one
row between them and should be designed together.

**herdr already does all of it.** Measured against the pinned 0.8.0, not
assumed:

- `pane.rename` and `tab.rename` take a nullable `label`. Emoji work
  unmodified - `🔥 payments spike` and `🚀 release` both came back
  byte-identical.
- The field is **absent when unset**, so "has a custom name" needs no
  sentinel.
- **A custom name and the agent's own title coexist as separate fields.**
  Setting OSC 2 in a renamed pane left `label` untouched and filled
  `terminal_title` beside it. The daemon never overwrites one with the
  other, so the compatibility this card asks for is already the backend's
  behaviour and Muster only has to decide presentation.
- **The name survives a daemon restart; the title does not.** After
  `server.stop` and a fresh daemon, `label` came back on both the pane
  and the tab, and `terminal_title` was null - the shell restarted, so
  nothing had set one yet.

That last asymmetry is the design, handed over for free: **the user's
name is durable identity, the agent's title is volatile status.** Which
is exactly the two lines the sibling card wants - a first line that is
stable enough to learn, and a second that changes as work happens. So:

- Line one: the custom label when set, else `directory · harness` as
  today.
- Line two: the terminal title, still shown for a named pane - naming
  something must not cost you the ability to see what it is doing.
- A tab caption takes its own label the same way, over herdr's
  workspace-and-number default.

**Muster drops the field at the seam today.** `Pane` in
`mirror/backend.rs` carries `id`, `agent` and `cwd` and no label, while
`Tab` and `Workspace` both have one. So the tab half is nearly free and
the pane half needs the field added.

**The real cost is that Muster has no text input anywhere.** No dialog,
no sheet, no editable field - this would be the first, and that is the
part to think about rather than the rename call. Options:

- **Inline edit in the sidebar row** (double-click, Finder-style). Lean:
  this is where you are already looking at the list and deciding which is
  which, and it needs no new window.
- An action with a chord opening a small sheet. More discoverable, more
  chrome, and a second place the same thing happens.
- Nothing in the GUI at all: `herdr pane rename` already works from
  inside a pane, because panes inherit `HERDR_SESSION`. That is the
  zero-cost path that exists right now, and it is worth saying out loud
  that it is not good enough - a person should not need the daemon's CLI
  to name their own window.

Emoji entry is free either way: ⌃⌘Space opens the picker in any real
`NSTextField`, so this needs no picker of Muster's own.

One thing that falls out of view = f(daemon state) and is worth keeping:
any client can rename, including herdr's own TUI, and the name simply
arrives. Nothing here should be Muster-local state, and clearing a name
is `label: null` rather than an empty string.
title: ✏️ Name a pane or a tab yourself, and have the name stick
